root_cause.text: The vulnerability exists because the ALSA ctxfi driver's `ct_vm_map()` function ignores the increased `CT_PTP_NUM` setting and only maps to the first page table area (`vm->ptp[0].area`), leading to out-of-bounds memory access when aggregate allocations exceed the capacity of that single page.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description explicitly states that "ct_vm_map() always uses PTEs in vm->ptp[0].area regardless of CT_PTP_NUM" and that exceeding the single page limit (512 PTEs on AMD64) causes the function to "access beyond the allocated space and causes a page fault," while the patch fixes this by reverting `CT_PTP_NUM` from 4 back to 1.

vuln_statements.explanation: Based on the vulnerability root cause, the ct_vm_map() function exclusively accesses vm->ptp[0].area regardless of CT_PTP_NUM setting. When aggregate allocations exceed the capacity of the first page table area, this causes out-of-bounds memory access. The fix would need to properly iterate through all page table areas up to CT_PTP_NUM rather than hardcoding index 0.
